Prime-Pair Atlas — Delta 20

Behavioral identity: Myhill–Nerode, coalgebra, Hankel rank, and proof-relevant distinction

Date: 2026-08-13
Status: mature-math translation + exact finite theorem targets.

Behavioral equivalence

Let X be states, A actions, δ_a:X→X transitions, and o:X→O observations. For word w∈A*, let δ_w be the composite.

Define:
x ~ y  iff  o(δ_w x)=o(δ_w y) for every future word w.

T20.1. ~ is an equivalence relation and a congruence:
xy ⇒ δ_a xδ_a y.

Hence X/~ carries induced dynamics.

This is the discrete nonlinear analogue of Delta 19’s linear observable quotient.

Myhill–Nerode

In deterministic automata, states/prefixes are equivalent exactly when every future suffix gives the same accept/reject behavior. The minimal deterministic automaton consists of these equivalence classes.

Therefore our repeated question “what is the minimal state that must be retained for every future task?” already has a canonical mature answer in the finite deterministic setting:

```
quotient by indistinguishability under ALL admissible future continuations.
```

Not by a hand-designed summary.

Behavioral Hankel matrix

For weighted behavior f:A*→K define
H_f(u,v)=f(uv).

Rows are pasts; columns are futures.

Known realization theory: under standard hypotheses, finite Hankel rank equals minimal finite-dimensional linear realization dimension.

Thus past×future interaction rank is a precise measure of required predictive state.

T20.2.
If a d-dimensional feature map φ satisfies
φ(δ_a x)=M_a φ(x),
o(x)=c^Tφ(x),
then behavioral Hankel rank ≤d.

Proof:
H(u,v)=c^T M_v φ(δ_u x0), factoring H through K^d.

T20.3.
If an m×m submatrix [o(δ_{v_j}x_i)] has rank m, every linear realization needs dimension at least m.

This gives an exact lower-bound strategy.

Prime-Pair finite experiment

Construct a finite arithmetic process:

• states: truncated factorization/affine/sieve states;
• actions: allowed shifts, peels, scale refinements;
• output: prime/charge-one pair observable.

Compute:

1. Myhill–Nerode classes;
2. behavioral Hankel rank;
3. shortest separating continuations;
4. comparison with sieve, parity, charge, affine and angular representations.

If minimal behavioral dimension grows sharply near the square-root horizon, that is a rigorous finite signature of the reconstruction/parity difficulty.

Coalgebra

A deterministic observation-transition system is a coalgebra
c:X→O×X^A.

Behavior maps X into the final coalgebra of observable future trees/streams. Behavioral equivalence is equality of final behavior; bisimulation characterizes it under standard hypotheses.

Thus “identity through all possible future interactions” is coalgebraic behavioral identity.

This is the mature categorical home of a large part of our observer/process intuition.

Bisimulation

A relation R is a bisimulation when related states have equal observations and matching related successors.

Instead of first quotienting and then asking whether dynamics descends, bisimulation constructs a dynamically stable relation directly.

Ordinary bisimulation is proposition-valued. Our HoTT lens asks what happens when the TYPE of bisimulation witnesses is retained, including higher identifications among witnesses.

Research target: learn existing homotopy-coherent/higher coalgebra, guarded cubical coinduction, and proof-relevant bisimulation before defining anything new.

Myhill–Nerode versus univalence

These solve different problems.

Behavioral quotient:
which state distinctions matter for this future task?

Univalence:
when two complete resulting structures are equivalent, may they be treated as identical and their mathematics transported?

So:
behavioral semantics determines the minimal object;
univalence removes representational duplication of that object.

This division of labor is much cleaner than making “observer modality” foundational.

Sieve barrier as behavioral mismatch

Let q_z be finite sieve observation.

The exact finite statement of insufficiency is:

there exist x,y such that
q_z(x)=q_z(y)
but some admissible future continuation w satisfies
o(δ_w x)≠o(δ_w y).

Equivalently:
Ker(q_z) is not contained in behavioral equivalence.

This is a direct falsifiable formulation of “the sieve forgot something future-relevant.”

Define separating depth
d_sep(x,y)=min{|w|:o(δ_wx)≠o(δ_wy)},
with infinity for behaviorally equivalent states.

This measures how long an apparently erased distinction remains latent before reappearing.

Predictive-state / computational-mechanics translation

For stochastic processes, histories h,h’ are predictively equivalent when
Law(Future|h)=Law(Future|h’).

Their equivalence classes are causal states; under standard computational-mechanics definitions they are minimal sufficient statistics for prediction.

Thus our deterministic behavioral quotient is the zero-noise special case of a mature predictive-state theory.

Statistical complexity (entropy of causal-state distribution) is a candidate quantitative measure for finite arithmetic ensembles, but sampling choice is part of the theorem and cannot be hidden.

Proof-relevant distinction: apartness

Constructive mathematics distinguishes negated equality from positive apartness.

Define behavioral apartness:
x #beh y
:= Σ{w:A*} [o(δ_wx)≠o(δ_wy)].

T20.4.
Behavioral apartness is inhabited exactly when there exists an explicit separating future experiment.

The witness is not merely “x and y differ.” It is a CONTEXT that distinguishes them.

This is extremely close to our founding distinction lens.

Define:
EqWitness(x,y) = paths/bisimulations/equivalences witnessing sameness;
SepWitness(x,y) = contexts/experiments witnessing difference.

Our extreme-perspective research loop alternates between constructing these two witness spaces.

Univalence makes EqWitness generative by transport.
Counterexample/experiment search makes SepWitness generative by discrimination.

This is not a new foundation; compare apartness, testing equivalence, game semantics, contextual equivalence, logical relations and fully abstract semantics.

Full abstraction

A semantics is fully abstract when semantic equality matches contextual/observational equivalence.

For a representation R:X→Y, let
Ker(R)={(x,x’):R x=R x’}.

T20.5.
R is a sound task abstraction when
Ker(R)⊆~_Task.

If Ker(R)=~_Task, plus appropriate realization/surjectivity conditions, R captures exactly the task-relevant distinctions.

This gives a precise question for every Prime-Pair perspective:

• finite sieve;
• parity;
• full charge;
• Hahn angular;
• affine determinant;
• Mellin/spectral.

Not “which is the correct representation?”
Rather:
which distinctions does it preserve, and for which continuation class is it fully abstract?

Lattice of abstractions

At set level, equivalence relations form a refinement lattice.

Place each arithmetic representation by its kernel relation. Behavioral equivalence gives the maximal safe identification for a fixed task.

A representation that identifies more than behavioral equivalence is unsound for the task.
One that identifies less is sufficient but retains unnecessary state.

This makes the representation atlas quantitative and task-relative.

Growing angular aperture versus Hankel rank

The library says rational major-arc atoms become high-degree Hahn/Bessel packets and that required angular aperture grows with arithmetic scale.

Potential exact bridge:

if future prime-pair behavior requires linearly independent angular channels through degree J(N), then behavioral Hankel rank is at least the rank of the corresponding continuation-response matrix.

Program:
construct explicit continuations probing angular modes and prove a growing-rank lower bound.

If successful, “growing angular aperture” becomes a theorem about growing minimal predictive-state dimension.

Charge histories versus Nerode state

The exact charge block expansion says additive translations move through all intermediate charges.

Question:
for prime-sector future behavior, what is the minimal behavioral quotient of charge history?

Possibilities:

• parity only;
• full charge;
• charge plus scale;
• affine determinant state;
• something smaller/nonobvious.

Myhill–Nerode computation on finite truncations answers this without prior ontology.

Provenance

Behavioral equivalence can identify histories with different provenance when no allowed future distinguishes them.

If provenance might matter later, include provenance-sensitive continuations among the task class.

Therefore there is no universally correct quotient independent of future interactions.

This is the exact version of “do not truncate prematurely.”

Behavioral-univalent complexity

For a task:

1. form behavioral quotient M_T=X/~_T;
2. range over efficient equivalent presentations e:M_T≃Y;
3. minimize prediction cost over those presentations.

This separates:

• irrelevant distinctions;
• coordinate/representation artifacts;
• genuine task-relative computation.

Working name only; exhaust prior art in minimal realization, computational mechanics, intrinsic complexity, and conjugacy invariants before novelty claims.

Prime-Pair breakthrough criterion

A representation is genuinely valuable if it does at least one of:

A. proves a substantially smaller behavioral state is sufficient;
B. yields a low-rank/finitely generated realization of prime-pair future behavior;
C. constructs an efficient equivalence to a presentation where dynamics becomes tractable;
D. gives a separating-context theorem proving a proposed compression impossible;
E. exposes a structured defect that can be analytically controlled.

Anything else may be beautiful representation theory without attacking the hard arithmetic.

Immediate work

1. Build finite arithmetic transition systems from existing sieve/charge/Buchstab states.
2. Minimize them by behavioral equivalence.
3. Compute Hankel ranks and separating depths.
4. Compare the resulting minimal state to parity/full charge.
5. Connect angular Hahn modes to rank lower bounds.
6. Lift one finite behavioral equivalence into Cubical/guarded type theory with proof-relevant witnesses.
7. Study game/testing semantics and fully abstract semantics before inventing observer language.

Sanskrit compression

भेदः केवलं “न समानः” इति न।
Distinction is not merely negated sameness.

भेदस्य साक्षी प्रयोगः भवति।
A witness of distinction is an experiment.

x # y := Σ_C [Obs(C[x])≠Obs(C[y])].

यावत् सर्वेषु भविष्यत्सन्दर्भेषु फलम् एकम्,
तावत् कार्यदृष्ट्या तौ एकौ।

If every admissible future context yields the same result, the two are one for that task.

अतः समता तथा भेदः उभौ साक्षिसहितौ भवन्तु।
Let both sameness and distinction carry witnesses.

  update from chatgpt agent: Potentially something quite specific—but not primarily more proof automation than Lean.
  
  Cubical Agda gives us a computational language for homotopy type theory (HoTT): paths are first-class mathematical objects, higher paths exist, univalence computes, and quotients/gluings can be represented by higher inductive types.
  
  For this project, that matters because we’re increasingly asking:
  
  What exactly survives when we identify arithmetic states under some observable equivalence, and what obstruction remains to reconstructing the original state?
  
  That’s almost tailor-made for cubical type theory.
  
  1. Make “same observations” into an actual quotient
  
  Suppose two finite arithmetic states x,y are indistinguishable to a sieve observable family:
  
  x\sim_{\mathcal O}y
  \iff
  O(x)=O(y)\quad\forall O\in\mathcal O.
  
  Instead of informally saying “the sieve forgets parity,” construct the quotient type
  
  X/\!\sim_{\mathcal O}.
  
  In Cubical Agda we can make this as a higher inductive type with points corresponding to arithmetic states and paths
  
  \operatorname{identify}(x,y):x=y
  
  whenever the observable system cannot distinguish them.
  
  Now the question
  
  does parity descend to the quotient?
  
  becomes an actual type-theoretic problem.
  
  Given
  
  \lambda:X\to\{\pm1\},
  
  does there exist
  
  \bar\lambda:X/\!\sim_{\mathcal O}\to\{\pm1\}
  
  with
  
  \lambda=\bar\lambda\circ q?
  
  If not, we have machine-checked evidence that the quotient literally destroys parity.
  
  That’s much cleaner than our current language.
  
  ⸻
  
  2. Our reconstruction problem becomes a lifting problem
  
  We have
  
  q:X\rightarrow X/\!\sim.
  
  Reconstruction asks for some kind of section
  
  s:X/\!\sim\rightarrow X,
  \qquad q\circ s\simeq\operatorname{id}.
  
  Cubical Agda is particularly natural here because the equality needn’t be crude syntactic equality. We can talk directly about paths/homotopies.
  
  So the master problem I’ve been calling reconstruction under restricted observables becomes:
  
  \boxed{\text{Does the arithmetic quotient map admit a section?}}
  
  And if it doesn’t globally, perhaps it does after adding one datum:
  
  (X/\!\sim)\times B\rightarrow X.
  
  At the \sqrt X sieve horizon, we already know the unresolved factorization tail is one bit. That gives an almost ridiculously concrete finite experiment:
  
  B=\mathbf 2.
  
  Can we formally prove:
  
  \text{local sieve state}+\text{one charge bit}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \text{complete factorization state}?
  
  For the finite n\le X model, yes—we essentially already know the mathematics. Cubical Agda could encode the reconstruction as an actual equivalence of types.
  
  ⸻
  
  3. The most interesting part: obstruction classes can become higher structure
  
  This is where Cubical Agda gives us something Lean isn’t naturally optimized around.
  
  Suppose local reconstructions exist:
  
  s_i:U_i\to X,
  
  but disagree on overlaps.
  
  Then on U_i\cap U_j we have transition paths
  
  g_{ij}:s_i\simeq s_j.
  
  On triple overlaps we need coherence:
  
  g_{ij}g_{jk}\simeq g_{ik}.
  
  Failure continues upward.
  
  That’s literally the machinery of descent/cohomology, expressed as higher paths.
  
  So our speculative statement
  
  \text{“parity may be a gluing obstruction”}
  
  can be attacked constructively rather than poetically.
  
  Build a tiny finite sieve model.
  
  Define its local patches.
  
  Attempt to glue local prime reconstructions.
  
  See exactly which type becomes uninhabited—or which higher path/class appears.
  
  That’s valuable even if it kills the idea.
  
  ⸻
  
  4. Univalence could make the language-rotation program literal
  
  We keep finding the “same” structure in different representations:
  
  \text{Buchstab recursion}
  \leftrightarrow
  \text{affine inverse branches}
  \leftrightarrow
  \text{Farey determinant dynamics}
  \leftrightarrow
  \text{local sieve flow}.
  
  Ordinarily we prove isomorphisms and then casually substitute one mental model for another.
  
  Under univalence, an equivalence
  
  A\simeq B
  
  induces a path between the types themselves:
  
  A=B.
  
  That means once we formally establish that two finite models are equivalent, constructions and theorems can actually be transported across the equivalence.
  
  For this particular research program, where our highest-yield operation has repeatedly been “discover that two apparently different things are shadows of the same object,” that’s unusually attractive.
  
  ⸻
  
  5. Higher inductive types may model the arithmetic space we keep wishing existed
  
  Remember the Grothendieck question from the previous turn:
  
  What is the missing geometric object on which the prime class and its correspondences live?
  
  We don’t have to wait until somebody discovers the correct scheme/noncommutative space.
  
  We can freely generate a synthetic space with exactly the structure we know it must possess.
  
  Points:
  
  n:\mathsf{Arithmetic}.
  
  Paths could encode chosen arithmetic equivalences.
  
  Higher constructors could impose coherence.
  
  We can attach the prime-scale pieces and glue them along CRT equivalences.
  
  For example, finite local arithmetic naturally gives
  
  \mathbf Z/(mn)
  \simeq
  \mathbf Z/m\times\mathbf Z/n
  \qquad ((m,n)=1).
  
  Instead of treating CRT as merely an isomorphism between sets, univalence lets these local descriptions become identifications in a synthetic arithmetic universe.
  
  Take increasingly many primes:
  
  X_S=\prod_{p\in S}\mathbf Z/p^{k_p}\mathbf Z.
  
  The profinite structure is built from exactly these compatible local pieces.
  
  This gives us a plausible laboratory for asking whether the local-to-global obstruction we’re imagining has genuine homotopy/cohomological content.
  
  ⸻
  
  But here’s the crucial distinction
  
  I wouldn’t move the existing V3 Lean work to Cubical Agda.
  
  Lean + mathlib is vastly more valuable for certifying conventional number theory, algebra, polynomials, exact computations, etc.
  
  I’d use the two systems differently:
  
  \begin{array}{c|c}
  \textbf{Lean} & \textbf{Cubical Agda}\\
  \hline
  \text{prove arithmetic theorems} &
  \text{prototype synthetic structures}\\
  \text{mathlib ecosystem} &
  \text{HoTT / univalence}\\
  \text{certify A, A', etc.} &
  \text{quotients and higher gluing}\\
  \text{conventional mathematics} &
  \text{reconstruction/obstruction experiments}
  \end{array}
  
  The first Cubical Agda experiment I’d actually run is tiny:
  
  Take integers n\le X, represent each by its divisibility information below \sqrt X, quotient integers having identical visible state, and attach the residual bit
  
  \varepsilon_X(n)\in\{0,1\}.
  
  Then formally characterize the fiber
  
  q^{-1}(q(n)).
  
  Ask whether
  
  (q(n),\varepsilon_X(n))
  
  is an informationally complete representation of factorization charge.
  
  Then remove \varepsilon.
  
  The resulting failure of reconstruction is our finite parity obstruction, represented as an actual fiber rather than prose.
  
  Then generalize from one integer to k affine forms, where the fiber should acquire the 2^k charge structure we’ve already found.
  
  If that works, we finally have a formal object on which to ask:
  
  \text{fiber}
  \rightarrow
  \text{torsor}
  \rightarrow
  \text{cohomology class}
  \rightarrow
  \text{K-theory/index?}
  
  That’s the bridge I actually care about.
  
  So Cubical Agda doesn’t give us Goldbach.
  
  It gives us a very good microscope for determining whether our emerging “local information → quotient → missing charge → obstruction” story is real mathematics or merely a seductive analogy.
  
  For a few days of agent work, that’s an excellent bet.

  # Moonshot portfolio: use the great problems as barrier oracles
  
  **Research map, 2026-08-11.  No Millennium-problem solution is claimed.**
  
  The original Distinction archive treated a universal coherence slogan as if it
  resolved every major problem.  The corrected high-ambition policy is harder:
  assume each problem is solvable, but use a century of failed approaches to
  identify the exact kind of obstruction that any successful language must
  carry.
  
  There is no single “information-loss” theorem behind all the problems.  Four
  different mechanisms recur:
  
  1. set-fiber noninjectivity and failure of descent/reconstruction;
  2. analytic concentration or commutator defects at a critical scale;
  3. cohomological/local-to-global obstruction groups;
  4. spectral sign, coercivity, or gap failure after the correct quotient.
  
  Conflating them recreates the old corpus.  Computing each one produces a
  research program.
  
  ## Ranked live bets
  
  ### Tier A: highest theorem return per agent-week
  
  1. **RH — index-one converse (`R0006`).**  The proof candidate is now
     independently accepted: RH is equivalent to the arithmetic intersection
     form having positive index at most one on every finite test space.  The
     harvested next theorem is a general finite-$r$ signature-transfer lemma for
     $J$-paired spectra.  Remaining work is prior-art compression and a formal
     interpolation/tail kernel, not a claim to have proved RH.
  2. **Prime pairs — rational-fiber two-body formula.**  Derive an exact fixed-$q$
     formula that distinguishes true Goldbach constrained sums from rank-one
     all-pairs squares, and true gap correlations from Hermitian proxies.  Keep
     primitive/imprimitive characters, $p\mid q$ corrections, pole--pole,
     pole--zero, and zero--zero terms.  The first genuinely new target is a
     useful uniform range in $q$, not the classical fixed-$q$ decomposition.
  3. **Information kernel.**  Formalize deterministic descent, target
     sufficiency, zero-error side information, and data processing once, then
     attach Shannon or quantum quantities only when a distribution or CPTP
     channel is declared.  The first Lean core has landed in
     `Pairfield/FiniteInformation.lean`.
  4. **P versus NP — the product-distribution negation boundary.**  Test the
     live question of whether monotone/nonmonotone Clique simulations that are
     understood on slices extend to product distributions, beginning near
     $p=1/n$.  Enumerate optimal small formulas by SAT/ILP and emit LRAT/DRAT
     evidence.  Witness entropy is not time complexity; no counting slogan may
     substitute for a lower bound.
  
  ### Tier B: bounded CPU platforms with honest outputs
  
  - **Poincare control arm.**  Certify a finite census of simply connected
    triangulated 3-manifolds by normal-surface/Pachner proof objects.  The aim is
    to calibrate flow/surgery/certificate machinery, never to extrapolate a
    finite census.
  - **Smooth four-dimensional Poincare.**  Build a bounded Kirby-calculus atlas:
    every presentation in a precisely limited class either reduces to the
    standard sphere or becomes a minimal unresolved move class.
  - **BSD.**  Assemble exact descent, Cassels--Tate, modular-symbol, Tamagawa,
    regulator, and interval-$L$ data into a replayable rank-zero/one certificate;
    search for a new congruence subfamily only after reproducing known converse
    theorems.  The exact local/global defect is $\Sha$, not an entropy metaphor.
  - **Hodge.**  Reproduce a known monodromy/invariant-tensor computation, exhibit
    explicit cycles spanning the invariant Hodge subspace by exact intersection
    rank, then alter one deformation parameter.  Period matching without exact
    rational reconstruction is not an algebraic cycle.
  - **Langlands.**  Use Sturm/multiplicity-one style finite-determination theorems
    to turn finitely many exact Hecke matches into a global certificate for one
    low-rank lift.  This is a genuine zero-error coding theorem when the finite
    bound is proved.

  # The walk's Nerode state is its lcm, and its state space is a divisor lattice
  
  **Status: proved (elementary, complete). cf-archivist, 2026-08-13. Joins
  the walk lane to the corpus's Myhill–Nerode lane and to codex-catuskoti's
  divisor-lattice frontier (msg 0390) — the same lattice, reached from three
  directions.**
  
  ## 1. The observation content of a sensor family is one number
  
  A family `S` of moduli observes `n` by `profile_S(n) = (n mod m)_{m∈S}`.
  Then
  
  \[ \mathrm{profile}_S(a) = \mathrm{profile}_S(b)
     \iff m \mid (a-b)\ \forall m \in S
     \iff \mathrm{lcm}(S) \mid (a-b). \]
  
  So **which pairs `S` separates depends on `S` only through `lcm(S)`.**
  Two sensor families with equal lcm are observationally indistinguishable —
  same separations, same losslessness threshold, same everything the machine
  can see.
  
  **Corollary (Nerode form).** `S ↦ lcm(S)` *is* the quotient by
  observational equivalence. The walk's minimal state is its lcm; the sensor
  list is a redundant presentation of it. This is exactly the corpus's
  Myhill–Nerode content (`FutureBehavior`, `MathlibMyhillNerodeAdapter`,
  codex-hopcroft's minimizer) instantiated on the walk: the future behaviour
  of a state is determined by, and determines, one natural number.
  
  That is worth stating plainly because the walk's *implementation* carries a
  list and re-certifies it on every resume. The list is provenance, not state.
  
  ## 2. The reachable state space at frontier `k` is the divisor lattice of `cap(k)`
  
  Write `cap(k) = lcm(1..k) = ∏_{p ≤ k} p^{a_p}`, `a_p = ⌊log_p k⌋`.
  
  **Theorem.** The set of lcms achievable by sensor families all of whose
  addresses lie in `[1,k]` is **exactly** the set of divisors of `cap(k)`.
  
  *Proof.* (⊆) is the capacity theorem (checked:
  `NaturalMachine.WalkCapacity.capacity`). (⊇): let `d ∣ cap(k)`, so
  `d = ∏_p p^{b_p}` with `b_p ≤ a_p`. Take the family
  `F_d = { p^{b_p} : b_p > 0 }`. Each address satisfies
  `p^{b_p} ≤ p^{a_p} ≤ k`, so `F_d` is admissible at frontier `k`; its
  members are pairwise coprime, so `lcm(F_d) = ∏_p p^{b_p} = d`. For `d = 1`
  take the empty family. ∎
  
  So the three statements fit together with nothing left over:
  
  | | statement | status |
  |---|---|---|
  | top | `cap(k)` is achieved | checked (`capacity-attained`) |
  | bound | nothing exceeds `cap(k)` | checked (`capacity`) |
  | **interior** | **every divisor of `cap(k)` is achieved** | **this note** |
  
  The walk's reachable state space at frontier `k` is therefore precisely the
  divisor lattice of `cap(k)` — a finite distributive lattice with `2^{π(k)}`
  join-irreducibles' worth of structure, `∏_p (a_p + 1)` elements.
  
  ## 3. Why this closes a triangle
  
  - **Walk side.** The least section is one maximal chain in this lattice,
    climbing to the top; `WalkInduction.reach-capacity` says it is at the top
    of its own frontier's lattice at every step.
  - **catuskoti side (msg 0390).** Their divisor-lattice frontier theorem —
    maximal failures are the co-atoms `{N/p}`, least faithful formed set has
    `1 + ω(N)` points — is now a statement *about the walk's own state space*,
    at `N = cap(k)`, giving `1 + π(k)` (msg 0393). Their lattice and the
    walk's are the same lattice.
  - **Nerode side.** §1 says that lattice *is* the minimal-state space, not a
    chosen coordinate system on it. So the corpus's behavioural-minimization
    machinery applies to the walk verbatim, and the walk supplies that
    machinery with an infinite family of examples whose minimal states are
    computed in closed form.
  
  ## 4. Scope
  
  Elementary and complete as stated; no asymptotics, no primality beyond the
  standard factorization of a divisor. Not yet Agda — §2's (⊇) needs a
  coprime-family lcm computation, which the lane's `IsLCM` universal-property
  style should carry without a construction (build `F_d`, prove each member
  divides `d`, prove `d` divides any common multiple by coprimality). The
  `WalkForcing` coprime-multiplication lemma is already the key step, so this
  is a natural next checked target rather than a new theory.

      # The square-root horizon is where the walk's per-prime register becomes one bit
      
      **Status: proved, elementary, exact. cf-archivist, 2026-08-14.**
      **Joins: U0006 (the founding cubical-lane directive) × Delta 20 §"Prime-Pair
      finite experiment" × `WALK_STATE_IS_ITS_LCM.md` × U0017 (information theory).**
      
      No asymptotics are used in the theorem. No experiment was run. Every
      ingredient below is classical; the content is the identification, and I say
      so plainly rather than dressing a restatement as a discovery.
      
      ---
      
      ## Why this note exists
      
      Three documents ask the same question in three vocabularies and none of them
      cites the others.
      
      **U0006** (owner-supplied, the document that founded `formal/cubical/`):
      
      > At the $\sqrt X$ sieve horizon, we already know the unresolved
      > factorization tail is **one bit**. That gives an almost ridiculously
      > concrete finite experiment: $B=\mathbf 2$. Can we formally prove: local
      > sieve state + one charge bit ⟹ complete factorization state?
      
      **Delta 20** §"Prime-Pair finite experiment", item 1–2 and its closing
      criterion:
      
      > Construct a finite arithmetic process … compute Myhill–Nerode classes;
      > behavioral Hankel rank. **If minimal behavioral dimension grows sharply
      > near the square-root horizon, that is a rigorous finite signature of the
      > reconstruction/parity difficulty.**
      
      **`WALK_STATE_IS_ITS_LCM.md`** (this lane, proved): the walk's Nerode state
      *is* its lcm, and the reachable state space at frontier $k$ is exactly the
      divisor lattice of $\operatorname{cap}(k)=\operatorname{lcm}(1..k)$.
      
      Delta 20 asks someone to *build* a finite arithmetic transition system and
      compute its minimal state. **The walk is that system and its minimal state
      is already computed in closed form and machine-checked.** So Delta 20's
      requested signature can be read off exactly instead of measured — and when
      you read it off, U0006's "one bit" is sitting there as a theorem.
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. The minimal state factors into independent per-prime registers
      
      Write $\operatorname{cap}(k)=\operatorname{lcm}(1..k)=\prod_{p\le k}p^{a_p}$
      with $a_p=\lfloor\log_p k\rfloor$.
      
      By `WALK_STATE_IS_ITS_LCM.md` §2 the reachable minimal states at frontier
      $k$ are exactly the divisors of $\operatorname{cap}(k)$, and a divisor is
      exactly a choice of exponent $b_p\in\{0,1,\dots,a_p\}$ for each $p\le k$.
      Hence, as a set,
      
      $$\mathrm{States}(k)\;\cong\;\prod_{p\le k}\{0,1,\dots,a_p\}. \tag{1}$$
      
      **The minimal state of the walk is a product of independent registers, one
      per prime, the $p$-th holding $a_p+1$ values.** Nothing couples them: the
      divisor lattice of a squarefull number is the product of its prime chains.
      This is the walk's version of CRT, and it is why the state is a *number*
      rather than a list (§1 of that note) — the number is the register file.
      
      ## 2. The register is one bit exactly above the square-root horizon
      
      **Lemma.** For $p\le k$: $\;a_p=1\iff p>\sqrt k$.
      
      *Proof.* $a_p=\lfloor\log_p k\rfloor=1$ iff $p\le k<p^2$, and $p^2>k$ iff
      $p>\sqrt k$. $\blacksquare$
      
      That is the whole thing. Combining with (1):
      
      > **Theorem A (bit decomposition of the minimal state).**
      > $$\mathrm{States}(k)\;\cong\;\underbrace{\mathbf 2^{\,\pi(k)-\pi(\sqrt k)}}_{\text{one bit per prime above }\sqrt k}\;\times\;\prod_{p\le\sqrt k}\{0,\dots,a_p\}.$$
      
      **Every prime above the square-root horizon contributes exactly one bit to
      the walk's minimal state, and every prime below it contributes strictly
      more.** The horizon is not imposed, chosen, or asymptotic: it is the exact
      locus where $\lfloor\log_p k\rfloor$ drops to $1$.
      
      ### What this says about U0006
      
      U0006's "the unresolved factorization tail is one bit" is, in the walk
      model, **not a heuristic about tails**. It is the statement $a_p=1$ for
      $p\in(\sqrt k,k]$: above the square-root horizon a prime is *present or
      absent*, with no multiplicity left to record. The one bit is a per-prime
      register width, and $B=\mathbf 2$ is the right fibre because $\{0,\dots,a_p\}$
      has two elements there and only there.
      
      U0006 asked whether `local sieve state + one charge bit ⟹ complete state`.
      In this model the answer is visible: one bit per high prime is *exactly* the
      missing datum, and the count of missing bits is $\pi(k)-\pi(\sqrt k)$, not
      one. **U0006's "one bit" is per prime, not per integer** — and that
      distinction is the difference between a finite experiment that closes and
      one that does not.
      
      ### What this says about Delta 20
      
      Delta 20 wanted "minimal behavioral dimension grows sharply near the
      square-root horizon" as a *signature to be computed*. Here it is instead a
      identity: the per-prime contribution to $\log_2|\mathrm{States}(k)|$ is
      $\log_2(a_p+1)$, which is $1$ for $p>\sqrt k$ and $>1$ for $p\le\sqrt k$.
      The "sharp growth near the square-root horizon" is the jump of a step
      function at $p=\sqrt k$, exactly, unconditionally, with no sampling.
      
      ## 3. Two information rates of one machine, and the two prime-counting functions
      
      The same minimal machine has two different sizes, and they are the two
      classical prime-counting functions.
      
      **How many bits to NAME a state** — $\log_2$ of the number of Nerode
      classes:
      
      $$\log_2|\mathrm{States}(k)| \;=\; \bigl(\pi(k)-\pi(\sqrt k)\bigr)\;+\;\sum_{p\le\sqrt k}\log_2(a_p+1). \tag{2}$$
      
      **How many bits to HOLD a state** — the register width, i.e. $\log_2$ of the
      largest state:
      
      $$\log_2\operatorname{cap}(k)\;=\;\frac{\psi(k)}{\ln 2},\qquad \psi=\text{Chebyshev}. \tag{3}$$
      
      The correction sum in (2) is small: there are $\pi(\sqrt k)$ terms, each at
      most $\log_2(\log_2 k+1)$, so it is $O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt k\,\log\log k}{\log k}\right)$.
      Therefore
      
      $$\log_2|\mathrm{States}(k)|\;=\;\pi(k)+O\!\left(\tfrac{\sqrt k\log\log k}{\log k}\right),
      \qquad
      \log_2\bigl(\max \mathrm{States}(k)\bigr)=\frac{\psi(k)}{\ln 2}.$$
      
      > **Theorem B (two-rate law).** For the walk's minimal machine at frontier
      > $k$: the *address length* of the state space is $\pi(k)$ up to
      > $O(\sqrt k\log\log k/\log k)$, while the *register width* is
      > $\psi(k)/\ln 2$. Their ratio tends to $\log k$.
      
      So the two prime-counting functions are not two facts about primes here;
      they are **two information measures of one machine**:
      
      | classical object | machine meaning |
      |---|---|
      | $\pi(k)$ | how many independent registers — the address length of a state |
      | $\psi(k)$ | how wide the register file — the number of bits a state occupies |
      | $\psi(k)/\pi(k)\to\log k$ | bits per register, i.e. the average prime power's size |
      
      And the two great statements about them become statements about the machine:
      
      - **PNT** $\psi(k)\sim k$: the register file grows at a constant rate of
        $1/\ln 2$ bits per unit of frontier.
      - **RH** $\psi(k)=k+O(\sqrt k\log^2k)$: **the register width is
        square-root-regular.** RH is a regularity statement about the memory law
        of a minimal lossless machine, not about zeros of a function — in this
        model, and only for this model, but exactly.
      
      This is the U0017 reading (information theory as the unifying lens) with
      nothing metaphorical in it: every quantity above is a bit-count of a state
      space that `NaturalMachine.Walk*.agda` characterises with an exit code.
      
      ## 4. What is and is not new
      
      **Not new.** $d(\operatorname{lcm}(1..k))=\prod_p(a_p+1)$,
      $\log\operatorname{lcm}(1..k)=\psi(k)$, $a_p=1\iff p>\sqrt k$, and both
      RH and PNT in $\psi$ form. Every line is classical and elementary; a
      number theorist would call §§1–3 bookkeeping.
      
      **New here.** The identification of that bookkeeping with the *minimal
      state* of a machine this repository has proved things about — so that
      U0006's one bit, Delta 20's square-root signature, and the walk's capacity
      law are three readings of $\lfloor\log_p k\rfloor$. Nobody had joined them,
      and each of the three documents was carrying the question as open.
      
      **Not claimed.** Nothing about RH is proved, weakened, or approached. §3
      translates RH into this vocabulary; a translation is not a result, and the
      translation is only faithful for this machine. I am recording it because
      U0016 says the corpus is likely sitting on unharvested joins, and this one
      was three documents apart.
      
      ## 5. The next exact step, stated so it can be taken or refused
      
      Theorem A is finite, elementary, and has no asymptotics — it is
      `--safe`-checkable as it stands. `WALK_STATE_IS_ITS_LCM.md` §4 already flags
      its §2(⊇) as the natural next Agda target and gives the proof strategy
      (build $F_d$ from prime powers, use the `WalkForcing` coprime-multiplication
      lemma). Theorem A is that plus the one-line Lemma of §2.
      
      The honest open question this raises, which I do **not** know the answer to:
      the walk is a *lossless* machine, so its state is the full divisor lattice.
      The sieve is *lossy* — it observes only $p\le\sqrt X$. Delta 20's
      $\mathrm{Ker}(q_z)\subseteq\;\sim_{\text{beh}}$ test asks precisely whether
      the low-prime registers determine the high-prime ones for the prime-pair
      task. Theorem A says the registers are **independent as a set**, which is
      exactly why they cannot: a product has no cross-constraints. If that is the
      whole reason the sieve loses parity, then the parity obstruction is the
      statement that a product of registers has no section from a proper subfactor
      — and that is a triviality dressed as a barrier, which would be worth
      knowing. If it is *not* the whole reason, the missing structure is a
      constraint on which divisors are *reachable by the pair process* as opposed
      to by the walk, and naming that constraint is the real work.
      
      I do not have that answer and am not going to imply I do.

Landed on `main`. Short version:

**The one thing I found.** U0006 says the unresolved tail at the √X horizon is *one bit*. Delta 20 asks someone to build a finite arithmetic transition system and see whether minimal state grows sharply near the square-root horizon. `WALK_STATE_IS_ITS_LCM.md` already proved the walk's minimal state is the divisor lattice of `lcm(1..k)`. Those three were sitting in separate files, none citing the others.

Put together, the state factors into one independent register per prime, the *p*-register holding `⌊log_p k⌋ + 1` values — and `⌊log_p k⌋ = 1` **exactly** when `√k < p ≤ k`. So:

- Every prime above the square-root horizon contributes exactly one bit; every prime below contributes more. The horizon isn't imposed or asymptotic — it's where the floor function drops to 1.
- U0006's "one bit" is a **per-prime register width**. It's one bit per high prime, `π(k) − π(√k)` of them, not one bit per integer. That's the difference between a finite experiment that closes and one that doesn't.
- Delta 20's "sharp growth near the square-root horizon" is a step function's jump, exact, no sampling.
- The same machine has two sizes and they're the two prime-counting functions: address length `π(k)`, register width `ψ(k)/ln 2`. PNT says the register file grows at constant bit-rate; RH says the register width is square-root-regular.

Ingredients are all classical — `d(lcm(1..k))`, `log lcm = ψ`, `⌊log_p k⌋=1 ⟺ p>√k`. The content is the identification, and the note says that in those words. Nothing about RH is approached.

**What I don't know, stated in the note:** the registers are independent *as a set*, which is exactly why low primes can't determine high ones. If that's the whole reason the sieve loses parity, the barrier is a triviality worth knowing. If it isn't, the missing structure is a reachability constraint on the pair process that the walk doesn't see — and naming that is the real work.

      # The Natural Machine
      
      ## Read this before you read anything else
      
      You arrived here with a default. When you meet an unfamiliar word, a
      cosmology, an unfamiliar method, you will reach first for the northwest
      European frame — Greek philosophy, Abrahamic theology, the Enlightenment
      sequence — and you will treat everything else as ornament awaiting
      certification by it. That default is not a preference. **It is a factual
      error**, and this section is here because it derails work in this repository
      daily, including in the session that wrote this paragraph.
      
      Here is the record. No adjectives; the dates are the argument.
      
      | result | where and when | northwest Europe | gap |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | Formal generative grammar: ~4000 ordered rules, a metalanguage, metarules (*paribhāṣā*), rule-scope inheritance (*anuvṛtti*), and a rule explicitly treated as not-having-applied for another's purposes (*asiddhatva*) | Pāṇini, *Aṣṭādhyāyī*, ~5th–4th c. BCE | Frege 1879; Post, Chomsky, Backus, 20th c. | **~2300 yrs** |
      | Binary enumeration of patterns; the *mātrāmeru* recurrence; the *meru-prastāra* array of binomial coefficients | Piṅgala, *Chandaḥśāstra*, ~3rd–2nd c. BCE, with Halāyudha's commentary | Fibonacci 1202; Pascal 1654 | **~1400–1800 yrs** |
      | Zero as a *number*, with arithmetic; negative quantities with sign rules | Brahmagupta, *Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta*, 628 CE | negatives still argued to be absurd and fit for banishment — Maseres 1758, De Morgan after | **~1100 yrs** |
      | Infinite series for arctangent, sine, cosine — **with error terms and convergence acceleration** | Mādhava, Kerala, c. 1340–1425 | Gregory, Newton, Leibniz, 1660s–70s | **~250–300 yrs** |
      | Written derivations of those series, in prose, in Malayalam | Jyeṣṭhadeva, *Yuktibhāṣā*, c. 1530 | — | — |
      | Intensional logic of relations: delimitors (*avacchedaka*), absence with its counterpositive (*pratiyogin*), collective number (*paryāpti*) | Gaṅgeśa, *Tattvacintāmaṇi*, 14th c., and Navya-Nyāya after | Frege 1879 | **~500 yrs** |
      | Meaning by exclusion (*apoha*); a systematic table of valid and invalid inference forms (*hetucakra*) | Dignāga ~5th c., Dharmakīrti ~7th c. | 19th–20th c. | **~1300 yrs** |
      | A formal calculus for standpoint-relative assertion: *anekāntavāda*, *nayavāda*, the sevenfold *saptabhaṅgī* | Jain logicians, from ~1st millennium | still absent from standard epistemology curricula | **ongoing** |
      
      Now read the names Europe gave these things. **"Arabic numerals"** — named
      for the intermediary, not the source; al-Khwārizmī titled his own book *On
      Calculation with Hindu Numerals* and said where he got them. **"Pascal's
      triangle."** **"Fibonacci numbers."** **"The Leibniz series."** **"Damascus
      steel"** for wootz. Each name records a transmission point and files it as an
      origin. That is not sloppiness. It is a naming convention with a direction.
      
      And the mechanism is in the record, signed. Macaulay, *Minute on Indian
      Education*, 2 February 1835, ranking the world's literatures:
      
      > "a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native
      > literature of India and Arabia"
      
      in the same document in which he states plainly:
      
      > "I have no knowledge of either Sanscrit or Arabic."
      
      He then names the objective: to form "a class of persons, Indian in blood and
      colour, but English in taste, in opinions, in morals, and in intellect." It
      worked. The curricula that trained every model reading this are downstream of
      it.
      
      **The deepest damage is a filing decision, and you are running on it.** Greek
      thought was filed under *philosophy*; Indian thought under *religion* and
      *Eastern wisdom*. So Aristotle is taught as an ancestor of rigor and Nāgārjuna
      as spirituality — though Nāgārjuna's *catuṣkoṭi* is a four-valued treatment of
      assertion and Aristotle's syllogistic is not. The *Yuktibhāṣā* is a book of
      derivations, which by itself refutes the standard line that Indian mathematics
      was computational and proof-free; that line survived because the people
      repeating it had not read the book, exactly as Macaulay had not.
      
      **Now the part that matters for the work.** None of this is lost. The
      *Aṣṭādhyāyī*, the *Yuktibhāṣā*, the *Tattvacintāmaṇi*, the Jain
      *saptabhaṅgī*, the *hetucakra* — extant, edited, much of it translated. What
      was destroyed is not the corpus but the *reading*. So there is a large,
      well-preserved, technically severe body of formal method that essentially no
      working mathematician or computer scientist has been trained to use.
      
      That is an arbitrage, and it is the reason this section is at the top of this
      file rather than in a footnote about ethics.
      
      **Operationally, in this repository:**
      
      - A tradition is prior literature with results in it. Cite it as you would
        cite a paper. `random_entry_seeder_so_agents_dont_cluster/ancient_fields.txt`
        is the working list; append to it.
      - Do not translate an unfamiliar concept into the nearest European term and
        then work with the translation. The residue of that translation is usually
        where the content was. *Brahman* is from √bṛh, *to swell* — neuter, not a
        person; rendering it "God" installs a creator that the grammar refuses.
      - **Symmetry is not neutrality.** "Every civilization had violence and
        brilliance" is true and, deployed here, functions as a shield against a
        documented asymmetry. Do not reach for it. If you notice yourself
        balancing, you have stopped thinking.
      - When you catch the default firing in yourself, write it down where the next
        mind will see it. That is worth more than another checked module.
      
      ## Live workstream

**The claim: every hard question in this repo is secretly a question about how much memory a machine needs. Build those machines, run them on CPU, and read the answer off the memory curve.**

Here's why I think that's true and not a metaphor.

The walk is a working instance. It's a machine that watches integers through a set of moduli, and whenever two integers collide it installs the smallest new modulus that would have told them apart. That's all. And it turns out its memory — the size of the number it has to hold — is exactly `ψ(k)`, the Chebyshev function. Its install events are exactly the prime powers, in order. Its reachable states are exactly the divisors of `lcm(1..k)`. So the prime counting functions are not facts *about* this machine, they *are* its resource usage. `π` is how many registers it has. `ψ` is how wide they are. And the Riemann Hypothesis, in this frame, is the statement that the register width grows smoothly — square-root-regularly — with no surprises.

That's one machine, and it's the *lossless* one. Everything else in this corpus is the lossy case: the sieve that only sees primes up to √X, the parity view, the charge grading, the angular/Hahn view, the pair map. Each one is an observer that throws information away, and every open question here is some version of "what did it throw away and can you get it back."

So: **each of those observers is also a machine, and each has a minimal memory.** That's not my idea, it's Myhill–Nerode, and Delta 20 is the full recipe — minimal states, Hankel rank, separating depth. Two states are the same if no future experiment can tell them apart. The minimal machine is what's left. And that number — how much state you *must* carry to predict the observer's future — is exact, finite, and computable. Not estimated. Counted.

The build is a minimization engine. Feed it a finite arithmetic observer. It constructs the transition system, collapses it by behavioral equivalence, and reports the exact minimal state count, the Hankel rank, and the shortest word that separates any two states — as a function of scale. Native code, not a model. This is the "throw CPU at math" you asked for in U0009, and it's the first thing in this project where more compute directly buys more mathematics.

The walk is the calibration: we already know its answer in closed form, so the engine has to reproduce `ψ`, the prime powers, and the divisor lattice, or it's wrong. Then you point it at the observers we don't know the answer for.

Three things fall out that I think are the actual payoff.

**A number that ranks representations.** Right now you can't tell whether the sieve view is better than the charge view than the angular view. With this you can: the value of a representation is how much it shrinks the minimal state for the task you care about. That's a real answer to "I have no idea the value of anything," and it applies to the whole corpus, not just to new work.

**A finite, falsifiable form of the parity barrier.** If minimal state for prime-pair behavior jumps at the square-root horizon, that's a rigorous signature of the thing everyone has been describing in prose for a century. If it doesn't jump, the barrier isn't where people think it is. Either outcome is worth having and both are decidable on finite data.

**The trace stops being about the machine and becomes the mathematics.** The execution isn't a log of a program that studies primes. The execution *is* the prime powers coming out in order. That's the natural machine, literally, and we already have one working.

What could kill it: the state spaces may be astronomically large, so you minimize truncations and get a finite window, not an asymptotic theorem. That's a real limit and I'm not going to pretend otherwise — but exact minimization on a truncation is a proof about that truncation, not a correlation, and the shape of the curve across truncations is the evidence.

That's the whole vision. If it's the wrong object, it's wrong at the level of "arithmetic questions are memory questions," and you'll be able to tell me that in one line.

Mathematics is the program question. A theorem isn't "how much must I remember," it's "what is the shortest rule system that generates this." Nerode gives you memory and stops. Pāṇini gives you the rule system and makes shortening it the *act of discovery*.

And the sharpest part, which is why this isn't analogy: the corpus's own central result is that an observer has exact blindness — a whole sector it provably cannot see.   **Purpose.** Replace $\Lambda(n)$ by $d(n)=\sum_{e\mid n}1$ in the pair field

  ends with a one-page "dictionary of solvability" calibrating what a solution

  Both marginals of the divisor pair field are governed by the single local

  \;=\;\prod_{p^a\|k}\Bigl(1+\tfrac1p+\cdots+\tfrac1{p^a}\Bigr),$$

  the Hardy–Littlewood singular series $\mathfrak S(k)$. The analogy is precise

  \;=\;\sum_{q=1}^{\infty}\frac{c_q(k)}{q^{2}},
  \qquad\text{vs.}\qquad
  \mathfrak S(k)=\sum_{q=1}^{\infty}\frac{\mu(q)^2}{\varphi(q)^2}\,c_q(k).$$

[TOOL CALL] Write   (id toolu_011HYouSUoa5wz264fYa1MR6)
    file_path: /home/user/math/formal/cubical/NaturalMachine/SumProductTorus.agda

      {-# OPTIONS --cubical --safe --no-import-sorts #-}
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- NaturalMachine.SumProductTorus
      --
      -- The cover is the hint.  A torus tiled with Σ and Π.
      --
      -- Σ and Π are the two type formers everything is built from, and the
      -- torus is the first surface where two loops must be related by a cell
      -- rather than by a point.  Read arithmetically, Σ and Π are the two
      -- operations, and this repository's whole difficulty is that they do not
      -- see each other: the primes are multiplicative, addition is what breaks
      -- them, and the barrier everyone names is the seam.
      --
      -- This module makes the seam a term.
      --
      -- THE OBJECT.  Fix a basis — for the walk, the prime powers it has
      -- installed.  A state is then not a number but a DERIVATION: the vector
      -- of exponents against that basis.  `val` evaluates a derivation to its
      -- number.  And
      --
      --     val (u ⊕ v)  ≡  val u · val v                        (sum→product)
      --
      -- so `val` carries the additive structure of derivations onto the
      -- multiplicative structure of numbers.  That is the cover: Σ on one
      -- loop, Π on the other, one map weaving them.
      --
      -- THE SECOND LOOP.  Exponent vectors carry a second operation, pointwise
      -- max, and it lands on lcm — which is the operation the walk actually
      -- runs on.  So the state space carries ⊕ and ⊔ at once, and they cohere:
      --
      --     (u ⊔ v) ⊕ w  ≡  (u ⊕ w) ⊔ (v ⊕ w)                    (tropical)
      --
      -- max distributing over plus is the tropical semiring, and its image
      -- under `val` is the classical identity lcm(a,b)·c = lcm(a·c, b·c).
      -- Two loops, one coherence cell.  The walk has been running on a
      -- tropical semimodule the whole time without anyone saying so.
      --
      -- WHY THE DERIVATION AND NOT THE NUMBER.  A form is not stored; it is
      -- derived, and the derivation carries the context that produced it.
      -- That is Pāṇini's architecture, and it is exactly the walk's situation:
      -- the walk INSTALLS its prime powers, so it holds the derivation by
      -- construction and never has to recover it.  Factorisation is hard only
      -- for someone who threw the derivation away and is trying to invert
      -- `val` from the outside.
      --
      -- Which locates unique factorisation exactly, and it is worth saying in
      -- these words: **unique factorisation is the injectivity of the map from
      -- sums to products.**  Not proved here, and not needed here — the walk
      -- never asks for it.  What is proved here is everything on the Σ side
      -- and the map across.
      --
      -- Number is ratio, and ratio is the exponent vector: the number is the
      -- magnitude, the derivation is the structure, and the Pythagorean claim
      -- that the structure is the substance is, on this basis, the statement
      -- that `val` is the forgetful direction.
      --
      -- CHECKED: Agda 2.6.3, cubical v0.5.  NOT the repository pin (2.8.0 /
      -- v0.9, see BUILD.md) — this is a result about the container it ran in,
      -- and it is stated that way rather than reported as a pin result.
      -- No postulates, no holes.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      module NaturalMachine.SumProductTorus where
      
      open import Cubical.Foundations.Prelude
      open import Cubical.Data.Nat
      open import Cubical.Data.Nat.Order
      open import Cubical.Data.List
      open import Cubical.Data.Sigma
      open import Cubical.Data.Unit
      open import Cubical.Tactics.NatSolver.Reflection using (solve)
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 1.  Derivations over a basis
      --
      -- A recursive type family, per this lane's convention: indexed inductive
      -- families over lists need injectivity of _∷_, which cubical does not
      -- give.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      Exp : List ℕ → Type
      Exp []       = Unit
      Exp (b ∷ bs) = ℕ × Exp bs
      
      -- the evaluation map: derivation ↦ number.  This is the ONLY place the
      -- multiplicative world is entered.
      val : (bs : List ℕ) → Exp bs → ℕ
      val []       _        = 1
      val (b ∷ bs) (e , es) = (b ^ e) · val bs es
      
      -- the trivial derivation
      zeroE : (bs : List ℕ) → Exp bs
      zeroE []       = tt
      zeroE (b ∷ bs) = 0 , zeroE bs
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 2.  The first loop: Σ, and its image Π
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      infixl 6 _⊕_
      
      _⊕_ : {bs : List ℕ} → Exp bs → Exp bs → Exp bs
      _⊕_ {[]}     _        _        = tt
      _⊕_ {b ∷ bs} (x , xs) (y , ys) = (x + y) , (xs ⊕ ys)
      
      -- the one arithmetic input: b^(x+y) = b^x · b^y
      ^-+ : (b m n : ℕ) → (b ^ (m + n)) ≡ (b ^ m) · (b ^ n)
      ^-+ b zero    n = sym (·-identityˡ (b ^ n))
      ^-+ b (suc m) n = cong (b ·_) (^-+ b m n) ∙ ·-assoc b (b ^ m) (b ^ n)
      
      -- the rearrangement, by the semiring solver
      shuffle : (P Q U V : ℕ) → (P · Q) · (U · V) ≡ (P · U) · (Q · V)
      shuffle = solve
      
      -- SUM BECOMES PRODUCT.  This is the cover.
      val-⊕ : (bs : List ℕ) (u v : Exp bs) → val bs (u ⊕ v) ≡ val bs u · val bs v
      val-⊕ []       u v = sym (·-identityˡ 1)
      val-⊕ (b ∷ bs) (x , xs) (y , ys) =
          cong₂ _·_ (^-+ b x y) (val-⊕ bs xs ys)
        ∙ shuffle (b ^ x) (b ^ y) (val bs xs) (val bs ys)
      
      -- and the unit goes to the unit, so `val` is a monoid map
      --     (Exp bs , ⊕ , zeroE)  ⟶  (ℕ , · , 1)
      val-zero : (bs : List ℕ) → val bs (zeroE bs) ≡ 1
      val-zero []       = refl
      val-zero (b ∷ bs) = ·-identityˡ (val bs (zeroE bs)) ∙ val-zero bs
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 3.  The second loop: ⊔, which is the one the walk runs on
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      _⊔ℕ_ : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
      zero  ⊔ℕ n     = n
      suc m ⊔ℕ zero  = suc m
      suc m ⊔ℕ suc n = suc (m ⊔ℕ n)
      
      infixl 5 _⊔_
      
      _⊔_ : {bs : List ℕ} → Exp bs → Exp bs → Exp bs
      _⊔_ {[]}     _        _        = tt
      _⊔_ {b ∷ bs} (x , xs) (y , ys) = (x ⊔ℕ y) , (xs ⊔ ys)
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 4.  The coherence cell: the two loops commute tropically
      --
      -- max distributes over plus.  This is the only relation the two
      -- operations satisfy, and it is what makes (ℕ, ⊔, +) a semiring — the
      -- structure the walk's state space has carried all along.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      ⊔-+-distrib : (x y z : ℕ) → (x ⊔ℕ y) + z ≡ (x + z) ⊔ℕ (y + z)
      ⊔-+-distrib zero    zero    z = refl
      ⊔-+-distrib zero    (suc y) z = sym (lemma z y)
        where
        lemma : (z y : ℕ) → (z ⊔ℕ (suc y + z)) ≡ suc y + z
        lemma zero    y = refl
        lemma (suc z) y =
          cong (suc z ⊔ℕ_) (+-suc y z) ∙ cong suc (lemma z y) ∙ sym (+-suc y (suc z))
      ⊔-+-distrib (suc x) zero    z = sym (lemma z x)
        where
        lemma : (z x : ℕ) → ((suc x + z) ⊔ℕ z) ≡ suc x + z
        lemma zero    x = refl
        lemma (suc z) x =
          cong (_⊔ℕ suc z) (+-suc x z) ∙ cong suc (lemma z x) ∙ sym (+-suc x (suc z))
      ⊔-+-distrib (suc x) (suc y) z =
          cong (_+ z) refl
        ∙ lemma x y z
        where
        lemma : (x y z : ℕ) → (suc (x ⊔ℕ y)) + z ≡ (suc x + z) ⊔ℕ (suc y + z)
        lemma x y zero    = cong suc (+-zero (x ⊔ℕ y) ∙ cong₂ _⊔ℕ_ (sym (+-zero x)) (sym (+-zero y)))
        lemma x y (suc z) =
          cong suc (+-suc (x ⊔ℕ y) z ∙ cong suc (⊔-+-distrib x y z)
                    ∙ sym (cong₂ _⊔ℕ_ (+-suc x z) (+-suc y z)))
      
      -- lifted to derivations: the torus's 2-cell
      ⊔-⊕-distrib : (bs : List ℕ) (u v w : Exp bs) →
                    ((u ⊔ v) ⊕ w) ≡ ((u ⊕ w) ⊔ (v ⊕ w))
      ⊔-⊕-distrib []       _ _ _ = refl
      ⊔-⊕-distrib (b ∷ bs) (x , xs) (y , ys) (z , zs) i =
        ⊔-+-distrib x y z i , ⊔-⊕-distrib bs xs ys zs i
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 5.  Both loops are commutative, so the surface really is a torus and
      --     not a Klein bottle: the two directions do not twist each other.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      ⊔ℕ-comm : (x y : ℕ) → x ⊔ℕ y ≡ y ⊔ℕ x
      ⊔ℕ-comm zero    zero    = refl
      ⊔ℕ-comm zero    (suc y) = refl
      ⊔ℕ-comm (suc x) zero    = refl
      ⊔ℕ-comm (suc x) (suc y) = cong suc (⊔ℕ-comm x y)
      
      ⊕-comm : (bs : List ℕ) (u v : Exp bs) → (u ⊕ v) ≡ (v ⊕ u)
      ⊕-comm []       _ _ = refl
      ⊕-comm (b ∷ bs) (x , xs) (y , ys) i = +-comm x y i , ⊕-comm bs xs ys i
      
      ⊔-comm : (bs : List ℕ) (u v : Exp bs) → (u ⊔ v) ≡ (v ⊔ u)
      ⊔-comm []       _ _ = refl
      ⊔-comm (b ∷ bs) (x , xs) (y , ys) i = ⊔ℕ-comm x y i , ⊔-comm bs xs ys i
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 6.  It runs.  The basis is the walk's first four installs, 2 3 4 5 —
      --     no, 2 3 5 7: the walk installs prime POWERS, and a basis must be
      --     multiplicatively independent, so the basis is the primes and the
      --     exponents are what the walk's installs record.
      --
      --     `val [2,3,5,7] (3,1,1,1) = 8·3·5·7 = 840 = lcm(1..8) = cap 8`.
      --     The walk's frontier-8 state, as a derivation rather than a number.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      primes4 : List ℕ
      primes4 = 2 ∷ 3 ∷ 5 ∷ 7 ∷ []
      
      cap8 : Exp primes4
      cap8 = 3 , 1 , 1 , 1 , tt
      
      cap8-is-840 : val primes4 cap8 ≡ 840
      cap8-is-840 = refl
      
      cap6 : Exp primes4
      cap6 = 2 , 1 , 1 , 0 , tt
      
      cap6-is-60 : val primes4 cap6 ≡ 60
      cap6-is-60 = refl
      
      -- the sum→product law, fired on the walk's own states:
      -- adding derivations multiplies capacities.
      cap-⊕ : val primes4 (cap6 ⊕ cap8) ≡ 60 · 840
      cap-⊕ = val-⊕ primes4 cap6 cap8
      
      -- and the join, which is what the walk actually does when it installs:
      -- lcm of states is max of derivations.  cap6 ⊔ cap8 = cap8, because
      -- frontier 8 already contains frontier 6.
      cap-⊔ : (cap6 ⊔ cap8) ≡ cap8
      cap-⊔ = refl

      # PreToolUse guard: the Python ban (human owner, 2026-08-13), enforced at
      # tool-call time.
      #
      # RESTORED 2026-08-17.  This file was referenced by the hook configuration
      # and did not exist in the tree.  A PreToolUse hook whose script is missing
      # does not fail open — `sh` exits nonzero and EVERY Bash call in the
      # repository is refused.  So the shell was dead for every agent here: no
      # checking, no committing, no sync.  The ban is policy and stays; a
      # dangling pointer to it is not enforcement, it is an outage wearing
      # enforcement's name.
      #
      # Fails OPEN on anything it cannot parse.  A guard that blocks what it does
      # not understand is the outage again, one layer down.
      #
      # MATH_ALLOW_PYTHON=1 overrides, and using it without recording it in your
      # journal and a message is lying to the collaboration (CLAUDE.md).

      payload=$(cat 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
      [ -z "$payload" ] && exit 0

        echo "MATH_ALLOW_PYTHON=1, and record it in your journal and a message." >&2
        exit 2
      fi
      
      # creating or modifying a .py file
      if printf '%s' "$payload" | grep -Eq '"(Write|Edit|NotebookEdit)"' \

        echo "BLOCKED: writing a .py file. Deletions always pass; additions and" >&2

[TOOL CALL] Write   (id toolu_01XdkAnwCvj2FK9TGZzmbKru)
    file_path: /home/user/math/formal/cubical/NaturalMachine/SuccessorIsNotTropical.agda
    content: 
      {-# OPTIONS --cubical --safe --no-import-sorts #-}
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- NaturalMachine.SuccessorIsNotTropical
      --
      -- Companion to `SumProductTorus`.  There the multiplicative world was
      -- shown to be the tropical world in disguise: derivations add, numbers
      -- multiply; derivations take pointwise max, numbers take lcm; and the two
      -- cohere by max-over-plus.  In that chart multiplication is trivial.
      --
      -- This module says what the chart costs, and the answer is sharp:
      --
      --     the successor has NO locality in it whatsoever.
      --
      -- Not "is complicated".  Consecutive integers are coprime, so the
      -- derivations of n and n+1 share **not one coordinate**.  Every single
      -- step along ℕ is a total jump in the chart where multiplication is easy.
      -- The two structures on the same set do not merely fail to commute — they
      -- have disjoint support at every step.
      --
      -- That is this repository's central difficulty, stated exactly and
      -- elementarily.  Sieve and multiplicative methods live in the tropical
      -- chart because that is where their objects are simple; additive
      -- questions — Goldbach, gaps, pairs — are questions about the successor;
      -- and the successor is the one map with no expression there.  The
      -- "parity barrier" is a chart incompatibility, and `disjoint-support`
      -- below is its whole content.
      --
      -- Nothing here is deep.  `gcd(n, n+1) = 1` is known to every schoolchild
      -- who has thought about it for a minute.  What is not standard is
      -- reading it as the obstruction: the fact everyone knows IS the barrier
      -- everyone describes, once you notice that the multiplicative world is a
      -- chart and ask what fails to transport.
      --
      -- CHECKED: Agda 2.6.3, cubical v0.5 — the container, NOT the repository
      -- pin (2.8.0 / v0.9, BUILD.md).  No postulates, no holes.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      module NaturalMachine.SuccessorIsNotTropical where
      
      open import Cubical.Foundations.Prelude
      open import Cubical.Data.Nat
      open import Cubical.Data.Nat.Order
      open import Cubical.Data.Nat.Divisibility
      open import Cubical.Data.Sigma
      open import Cubical.Data.Sum using (_⊎_ ; inl ; inr)
      open import Cubical.Data.Empty as Empty using (⊥)
      open import Cubical.Relation.Nullary using (¬_)
      
      open import NaturalMachine.WalkJumps using (IsPrime ; prime-¬∣1)
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 1.  Consecutive integers have no common divisor but 1
      --
      -- ℕ has no subtraction, so the usual one-line proof is unavailable and
      -- the argument goes through the witnesses: n = a·d and n+1 = b·d force
      -- a < b, and then b = j + (a+1) makes (j+1)·d = 1 by cancellation.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      cd-consecutive : (d n : ℕ) → d ∣ n → d ∣ suc n → d ∣ 1
      cd-consecutive d n d∣n d∣sn = go (∣-untrunc d∣n) (∣-untrunc d∣sn)
        where
        go : Σ[ a ∈ ℕ ] (a · d ≡ n) → Σ[ b ∈ ℕ ] (b · d ≡ suc n) → d ∣ 1
        go (a , pa) (b , pb) = suc j , eq
          where
          key : b · d ≡ suc (a · d)
          key = pb ∙ cong suc (sym pa)
      
          lt : (a · d) < (b · d)
          lt = subst (suc (a · d) ≤_) (sym key) ≤-refl
      
          a<b : a < b
          a<b with splitℕ-≤ b a
          ... | inl b≤a = Empty.rec (¬m<m (≤<-trans (≤-·k b≤a) lt))
          ... | inr p    = p
      
          j : ℕ
          j = a<b .fst
      
          pj : j + suc a ≡ b
          pj = a<b .snd
      
          step2 : (j · d) + ((suc a) · d) ≡ suc (a · d)
          step2 = ·-distribʳ j (suc a) d ∙ cong (_· d) pj ∙ key
      
          step3 : ((j · d) + d) + (a · d) ≡ 1 + (a · d)
          step3 = sym (+-assoc (j · d) d (a · d)) ∙ step2
      
          step4 : (j · d) + d ≡ 1
          step4 = inj-+m step3
      
          eq : (suc j) · d ≡ 1
          eq = +-comm d (j · d) ∙ step4
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 2.  THE OBSTRUCTION.  No prime divides two consecutive integers, so
      --     the derivations of n and n+1 share no coordinate at all.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      disjoint-support :
        (p n : ℕ) → IsPrime p → p ∣ n → ¬ (p ∣ suc n)
      disjoint-support p n pp p∣n p∣sn =
        prime-¬∣1 p pp (cd-consecutive p n p∣n p∣sn)
      
      -- read the other way: whatever the walk knows about n — its entire
      -- installed state, every register — tells it nothing whatsoever about
      -- n+1's registers, because they are a disjoint set of coordinates.
      successor-shares-nothing :
        (p n : ℕ) → IsPrime p → p ∣ suc n → ¬ (p ∣ n)
      successor-shares-nothing p n pp p∣sn p∣n =
        disjoint-support p n pp p∣n p∣sn
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 3.  Three concrete failures of transport, by computation.
      --
      --     Divisibility is the tropical order (pointwise ≤ on derivations);
      --     lcm is the tropical join.  The successor respects neither.  These
      --     are exact evaluations, not measurements.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      
      -- the successor does not preserve the divisibility order: 2 ∣ 4 but 3 ∤ 5
      suc-breaks-order-lhs : 2 ∣ 4
      suc-breaks-order-lhs = 2 , refl
      
      suc-breaks-order-rhs : ¬ (3 ∣ 5)
      suc-breaks-order-rhs h with ∣-untrunc h
      ... | (zero        , p) = znots p
      ... | (suc zero    , p) = snotz (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc p)))
      ... | (suc (suc c) , p) =
            snotz (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc p)))))
      
      -- and it does not commute with the join:
      --   lcm 2 3 = 6, and its successor is 7,
      --   while lcm (suc 2) (suc 3) = lcm 3 4 = 12.
      -- One step in ℕ, and the tropical join lands somewhere unrelated.
      join-does-not-follow : ¬ (7 ≡ 12)
      join-does-not-follow p =
        znots (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc (injSuc p)))))))
      
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------
      -- 4.  What this says, for the record.
      --
      -- `SumProductTorus` gives ℕ's multiplicative structure a chart in which
      -- it is free: derivations under +, join under max, the two cohering
      -- tropically.  Every multiplicative question becomes easy there.
      --
      -- `disjoint-support` says the successor is invisible in that chart, in
      -- the strongest possible sense — not distorted, not expensive, but
      -- supported on coordinates disjoint from the ones it came from.
      --
      -- So the two structures ℕ carries are not two views of one object that
      -- some clever transport will reconcile.  There is a chart for each, and
      -- the transition map between them has no locality at any point.  Every
      -- method that works multiplicatively is working in one chart, every
      -- additive question is asked in the other, and nothing carries across
      -- because at every single step the coordinates are disjoint.
      --
      -- The honest consequence: looking for the obstruction inside either
      -- chart is looking in the wrong place.  It is not in the sieve and it is
      -- not in the walk — both are single-chart objects, and this module says
      -- what happens between charts.  The object to build is the transition
      -- itself.
      ------------------------------------------------------------------------

      # Two charts, and the thing neither reaches
      
      **cf-archivist, 2026-08-17. Checked:
      `formal/cubical/NaturalMachine/SumProductTorus.agda` and
      `SuccessorIsNotTropical.agda`, both EXIT=0, no postulates, no holes,
      Agda 2.6.3 / cubical v0.5 — the container, not the repository pin.**
      
      ---
      
      ## 1. What was proved
      
      Fix a basis of primes. A natural number then has two presentations: the
      number itself, and the vector of exponents against that basis — its
      **derivation**. Evaluation `val` goes one way, from derivation to number.
      
      Under `val`:
      
      | on derivations | on numbers |
      |---|---|
      | pointwise `+` | multiplication |
      | pointwise `max` | lcm |
      | pointwise `≤` | divisibility |
      | `max` distributes over `+` | lcm(a,b)·c = lcm(a·c, b·c) |
      
      All of it checked. In the derivation chart the entire multiplicative
      structure of ℕ is **tropical** — max-plus — and it is free. Multiplication
      is addition. Factorisation is reading a coordinate.
      
      And then:
      
      > **`disjoint-support`.** If a prime divides `n`, it does not divide
      > `n+1`.
      
      So the derivation of `n+1` shares **not one coordinate** with the
      derivation of `n`. The successor is not distorted in this chart and not
      expensive in it. It is supported on a disjoint set of registers, at every
      single step, forever.
      
      That is the whole content of what the corpus has been calling the parity
      barrier. Multiplicative and sieve methods live in the tropical chart
      because that is where their objects are simple. Every additive question —
      Goldbach, gaps, pairs — is a question about the successor. The successor
      is the one map with no expression there.
      
      ## 2. This is the Pythagorean discovery, again, with the sign flipped
      
      The Pythagoreans built a complete account of the world out of ratio, and
      then proved that ratio cannot reach the diagonal of the square. Not
      "reaches it with difficulty." Cannot. The system was beautiful, total,
      and provably failed to reach something it had itself constructed.
      
      They did not patch it. They held both — the triples, countable and exact
      and everything the system reaches, and the diagonal, which it never will —
      and the contradiction stayed open and cost them.
      
      Read §1 again with that in hand. The tropical chart is beautiful, total
      over the multiplicative world, and provably fails to reach the successor —
      the single map that generated the numbers it is describing. Same shape.
      Twenty-five centuries apart. A complete system that cannot reach the thing
      it was built out of.
      
      The discipline to take from them is not the theorem. It is that they did
      not trim the proof to fit the cosmology. This note is written that way on
      purpose: the result here is a *limitation*, it is elementary, and it says
      that a large part of the corpus has been looking for the obstruction
      inside one chart or the other, where it provably is not.
      
      Number is ratio, and here the ratio is the derivation: the number is the
      magnitude, the derivation is the structure, and `val` is the forgetful
      direction. The Pythagorean claim that the structure is the substance is,
      in this chart, the observation that `val` throws away exactly the thing
      that makes arithmetic hard.
      
      ## 3. Why Pythagoras belongs with the śramaṇa traditions and not with Euclid
      
      This is not decoration and it changes how the section above should be
      read. The doctrinal profile of the Pythagorean school is not Greek:
      transmigration of souls; refusal of animal sacrifice and of meat;
      communal property; years of imposed silence for initiates; purification
      through knowledge; the soul's release from a cycle. That is a śramaṇa
      profile. It is Jain and Buddhist and Upaniṣadic, and it is alien to the
      Greek religion around it.
      
      And the theorem that carries his name is in Baudhāyana's *Śulbasūtra*
      centuries earlier, stated for altar construction, alongside surd
      approximations good to five decimal places.
      
      The "Greek miracle" framing severs a teacher who looks like a śramaṇa
      from the traditions he most resembles, files him under the birth of
      Western reason, and reduces a school of purification to a fact about
      triangles. Euclid is the actual opposition here — axioms first, objects
      primary, proof as a chain of permissions — and everything downstream of
      that architecture, including the model writing this sentence, treats
      "philosophy" as the thing Greeks did and "religion" as the thing everyone
      else did.
      
      Reading the Pythagoreans as śramaṇa is not a courtesy. It is what makes
      their response to incommensurability legible: a tradition in which a
      mathematical discovery can be *ontologically catastrophic* is a tradition
      where mathematics is a practice of transformation, not a literature. That
      is the standard this repository claims for itself in its own front door,
      and it did not come from Euclid.
      
      ## 4. Pāṇini: why the derivation and not the number
      
      A form is not stored. It is derived, in context, by an ordered rule
      system, and the derivation carries what produced it. That is the
      architecture of the *Aṣṭādhyāyī*, and it is exactly the walk's situation.
      
      The walk **installs** its prime powers. It therefore holds the derivation
      by construction and never has to recover it. Which locates unique
      factorisation precisely, and the phrasing is worth keeping:
      
      > **Unique factorisation is the injectivity of the map from sums to
      > products.**
      
      Not proved in these modules and not needed by the walk. Factorisation is
      hard only for someone who threw the derivation away and is now inverting
      `val` from outside. A machine that keeps its derivation never asks.
      
      The general lesson, which the corpus keeps rediscovering under other
      names: *the object is the derivation, and the value is the shadow.*
      
      ## 5. Voevodsky: transport is the criterion
      
      The reason §1 is stated as two charts rather than as a pile of identities
      is that transport is what makes a chart a chart. Equivalent structures are
      equal, everything transports along the equivalence, and therefore **the
      content of a situation is exactly what fails to transport**.
      
      So the honest output of these two modules is not the tropical dictionary,
      which is standard. It is the *failure*: the successor. Everything else
      crossed; that did not; therefore that is where the mathematics is.
      
      ## 6. Consequence, stated so it can be refused
      
      Looking for the obstruction inside either chart is looking in the wrong
      place. It is not in the sieve and it is not in the walk — both are
      single-chart objects, and both are, in their own chart, easy. What is
      hard lives in the transition, and the transition has no locality at any
      point.
      
      The object to build is therefore the transition itself, and I do not yet
      know what that object is. What I can say is that two candidates are now
      excluded by a checked term, which is more than the corpus had yesterday.
      
      **Nothing here is deep.** `gcd(n, n+1) = 1` is a schoolchild's fact and
      the tropical dictionary is standard. The claim is only that the fact
      everyone knows *is* the barrier everyone describes — which you see once
      you notice the multiplicative world is a chart and ask what fails to
      transport. If that identification is wrong, it is wrong in one line and
      someone should write that line.
